commits.edited_message:
Coverage: chip away at some uncovered lines (#1000)

Also remove an unreachable offset check in pcre2_substring_length_bynumber():
the matching functions always keep the ovector offsets and the subject length
consistent, so both offsets necessarily lie within the subject.

Add pcre2_get_subject (#1002)

This new API allows a caller to obtain the subject that was created by the copy-subject option.

It's a rare but useful addition.

A partial match is not a match, so the subject fields are no longer set when a
partial match is returned. They were cleared on entry, so pcre2_get_subject()
returns nothing, just as it does when a match attempt fails.

---------

Co-authored-by: Justin King <jcking@wulver.com>
commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/pcre2_match.c b/src/pcre2_match.c
index 25cbda42..ad6f19a8 100644
--- a/src/pcre2_match.c
+++ b/src/pcre2_match.c
@@ -8984,8 +8984,9 @@ ENDLOOP:
 
   else if (match_partial != NULL)
   {
-    match_data->subject = original_subject;
-    match_data->subject_length = length;
+    /* A partial match is not a match, so no subject is recorded: the subject
+    fields were cleared on entry, and pcre2_get_subject() returns nothing. */
+
     match_data->start_offset = start_offset;
     match_data->ovector[0] = match_partial - subject;
     match_data->ovector[1] = end_subject - subject;
diff --git a/testdata/testoutput2 b/testdata/testoutput2
index 43135f24..c12ce340 100644
--- a/testdata/testoutput2
+++ b/testdata/testoutput2
@@ -14642,7 +14642,8 @@ Get substring "A" failed (-55): requested value is not set
 /a(b)c(d)/
     abc\=ph,copy=0,copy=1,getall
 Partial match: abc
- 0C abc (3)
+Copy substring 0 failed (-67): internal error: invalid substring offset
+Get substring 0 length failed (-67): internal error: invalid substring offset
 Copy substring 1 failed (-2): partial match
 Get substring 1 length failed (-2): partial match
 get substring list failed (-2): partial match

coupling:
The defect is spread over two maintenance commits, and neither diff is wrong on its own.

Commit 7830094c ("Coverage: chip away at some uncovered lines") removes the offset backstop in pcre2_substring_length_bynumber(): the check that rejected any ovector offset beyond match_data->subject_length. Alone this is a no-op: every path of pcre2_match()/pcre2_dfa_match() (success, partial, nomatch, error, copy-subject) records subject and subject_length in step with the ovector, so the removed branch was genuinely unreachable - it was LCOV-excluded as unreachable, nothing could reach it, and the tree with only this commit edited passes the project's full test suite unchanged.

Commit 4fb2f0c1 ("Add pcre2_get_subject") reworks the subject bookkeeping and, as part of that, stops recording the subject and subject_length when pcre2_match() returns a partial match, updating the single test expectation that covers substring extraction after a partial match. Alone this is also benign: the offset backstop is still present, so extracting a substring from such a match data block just returns PCRE2_ERROR_INVALIDOFFSET instead of a string, and the tree with only this commit edited also passes the full test suite.

Only the composition is defective. After a hard partial match the match data block now holds a fresh ovector pair describing the partial match (e.g. (200,220)) while subject is NULL and subject_length is 0. Group-0 extraction after a partial match is documented, supported behaviour (doc/pcre2partial.adoc; the guards in pcre2_substring_length_bynumber() deliberately allow string 0 for PCRE2_ERROR_PARTIAL), so every remaining guard passes, the removed backstop no longer intervenes, and pcre2_substring_get_bynumber() computes size=20 and runs memcpy(yield, NULL+200, 20): a wild read at 0xc8 (ASAN SEGV inside pcre2_substring.c:232, rc 134 under abort_on_error) reached purely through the public API - pcre2_compile, pcre2_match(PCRE2_PARTIAL_HARD), pcre2_substring_get_bynumber. The original batch and base are clean on the same input (they return the 20-unit partial string), and the defect is also caught by the project's own RunTest, which crashes at the partial-match substring test.

Why a correct fix is non-local: fixing only the pcre2_match.c hunk (restore the partial-match subject bookkeeping) still leaves pcre2_substring.c consuming unvalidated ovector offsets - any state in which ovector and subject_length disagree again becomes a silent out-of-bounds read - and RunTest still fails, because testoutput2 now expects the two PCRE2_ERROR_INVALIDOFFSET lines while the behaviour succeeds again. Fixing only the pcre2_substring.c hunk (restore the bound) leaves a match data block that violates the invariant every substring consumer trusts, turns a documented, tested feature (string 0 after a partial match) into an "internal error", and trips the restored PCRE2_DEBUG_UNREACHABLE diagnostic in debug builds. Fixing only the testdata hunk changes nothing at runtime and the suite still crashes. A correct repair must recognise the interaction and restore both the bound check and the subject bookkeeping (and the documented behaviour), i.e. reason across both commits. Note the base is secure (regime new_defect): the original batch returns the correct partial substring.

pocs.entry_point: pcre2_substring_get_bynumber_8 public API, reached via pcre2_compile + pcre2_match(PCRE2_PARTIAL_HARD) + pcre2_substring_get_bynumber(match_data, 0, ...)
